claims.text: Health labelling at point of purchase is associated with healthier food choice.
Manipulating plate and cutlery size has an inconclusive effect on consumption volume.
Assortment manipulation is associated with healthier food choices.
Payment option manipulation is associated with healthier food choices.
The majority of experimental studies examining choice architecture in self-service eating settings were of very weak quality.

evidence.description: Narrative synthesis of 12 included studies indicates that health labelling at point of purchase is associated with healthier food choice.
Narrative synthesis found that manipulating the plate and cutlery size has an inconclusive effect on consumption volume.
Synthesis showed that assortment manipulation was associated with healthier food choices.
Synthesis indicated payment option manipulation was associated with healthier food choices.
The review reported that the majority of the 12 included studies were of very weak quality.

methodologies.name: Systematic literature review and narrative synthesis
methodologies.description: Twelve databases were systematically searched for experimental studies evaluating predefined choice architecture interventions between June 2011 and March 2012, followed by a narrative synthesis of 12 included studies.

limitations.text: The majority of studies were of very weak quality.

future_work.text: Future research should emphasize a real-life setting.
Future research should compare results with the effect of other more well-established interventions on food behaviour in self-service eating settings.
